correctness.rationale: The exact 3-by-3 Gauss quadrature and Verlet matrices specialize the published SDC position sweep. Its fixed-point stages yield the symplectic [2/2] Gauss endpoint determinant one. The finite-sweep error is a matrix-power recurrence with invariant 2D compression H and leading determinant defect (-1)^k qH^k c times z^(k+1). The trace starts at 2-z, so the two automatic Jury inequalities and determinant sign give the precise local stability dichotomy. H has conjugate eigenvalues with twice-angle cosine (sqrt(3)-1)/2; irrationality follows because the other conjugate of the root-of-unity trace sqrt(3)-1 lies below -2. Equidistribution gives half-density of each sign; a nonzero sinusoid with irrational phase has at most one zero index. The included checker independently reconstructs quadrature, six exact leading coefficients and nine high-precision sweeps. No infinite statement relies on finite testing.

value.rationale: The motivating primary study explicitly lacked a theoretical explanation for unpredictable harmonic SDC stability as the sweep count changes. This result provides a complete asymptotic classification for every sweep count on a natural smallest nontrivial Gauss–Legendre configuration, with an exact novel compression and a density theorem that rules out simple permanent odd/even heuristics. The half-density phenomenon concerns strict long-time numerical stability, not merely a cosmetic change in algebraic normalization. It has direct interpretive value for selecting finite correction counts; the setting and limitations are explicit and it does not overclaim global stability ranges or other schemes.
